summary: Processed-input estimator for chats without reported usage. Aggregate results only; no private identities, text or paths.

population.source: root Claude coding conversations in one library copy (claude-code, SDK and Conductor harnesses), half of the population by identifier prefix
population.split: stable family hash 60/20/20; forward-time set is the latest fifth of turns in families outside training
population.exclusions: requests at or after a conversation's first recorded compaction; conversations with more than one agent session; estimated rows

growth_fit.target: recorded input (cached and uncached) of a request minus that of the request before it
growth_fit.unit: tokens per 1,000 characters, or tokens per block for n_* terms
growth_fit.notes: Results longer than about 30,000 characters add no further input in coding harnesses, which truncate them; chat tool results carry no such evidence and are counted whole. Web tool results in coding are short summaries, so no web-specific rate is identified.

history_model_masked_boundaries.description: Request boundaries hidden; requests inferred from tool-result runs; rates from the growth fit; per-request overhead fitted on training turns

shipping_rule_replay.description: The published rule: one context rate for visible characters, the published per-call allowance, thinking retained across turns (0.681 tokens per visible thinking character stands in for the output model's thinking estimate), coding results truncated as the growth fit found.

thinking_retention: Request-level fits by model family give thinking from earlier user turns a positive input coefficient close to this turn's (about 0.5 to 0.9 of it) in every supported family but one, so the expected context keeps earlier thinking.
limits: Chat system prompts and tool definitions are unobserved: the expected value counts visible history only and understated recorded coding input by about 40%, where that overhead is known to be large.
Coding labels cannot validate chat retention, context editing or caching policy.
The cache division reproduces coding's recorded read share within about 1.3 points without a lifetime rule; the chat lifetime is an assumption.
The same extract supplied the fit and its tests; a fresh extract should precede any coefficient change.
